1.

By this award, I shall decide a claim petition under section 166/140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
filed by the petitioner Abdul Salam with respect to the injures caused to him in a vehicular accident
on 28.10.2020.

2. The facts of the case are that on that day, the petitioner Abdul Salam along with his brothers
Salimuddin and Fahimuddin and friends Zahid & Salman, were going to their home Rabupura after
attending a marriage ceremony in Bulandshahar by their car registration n.o Mh-14-Da- 0209.

When they reached near village Sikheda, a truck registration no. RJ-14GG-8661 (offending vehicle)
was coming from Bulandshahar.
The driver of the truck was driving it in a rash and negligent manner.
The truck hit their car and two other vehicles and caused the accident.
The driver of the truck was Raham Deen.
He is also the owner of the truck.
In that accident, Zahid and Salman died on the spot and the petitioner and his brothers injured.
The petitioner was taken to Babu Banarasi Das Hospital Meerut, from where he was referred to Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel Hospital.
According to the petition, the petitioner was treated in AIIMS Hospital and his treatment is still under going on.
The petitioner suffered permanent disability due to this accident.

As per his disability certificate,
he has 42% locomotor disability due to fracture and 30% ophthalmology disability in the left eye.

3. The respondent no.1 Raham Deen who is the driver and owner of the offending truck has taken the defence that the accident happened due to the fault of a third vehicle- a tempo, which tried to overtake his truck due to which he had to apply sudden breaks to save that vehicle and got overturned.
The respondent no. 2 insurance company has taken the general defences.
4. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties following issues were framed on 02.06.2022.

(i) Whether the Petitioner Abdul Salam suffered grievous injuries in a motor vehicular accident happened on 28.10.2020 at 5.00 p.m., near Village Sikheda,
Bulanshahar, U.P. within jurisdiction of PS Kotwali Dehat, due to rash and negligent driving of trailer (Tata motor 18 tyres) bearing registration No.RJ14GG8661 being driven by respondent No.1 /Rahamdeen?

(OPP) 
(ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation on account of said injuries and if yes, to what extent and from whom?

(OPP) 
(iii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate and for which period?

(OPP)
5.
In order to establish his claim, petitioner Abdul Salam has examined himself as PW-1 but the respondents did not lead any evidence.

sentences.text: I have heard Mr. Fakhruddin, counsel for petitioner, and Mr. Naved Rajpur counsel for respondent no. 1 and Ms. Sonali Aggarwal counsel for no. 2/insurer and perused the records.

7. The issues are decided as follows- ISSUE NO.1: Whether the Petitioner Abdul Salam suffered grievous injuries in a motor vehicular accident happened on 28.10.2020at 5.00 p.m., near Village Sikheda, Bulanshahar, U.P. within jurisdiction of PS Kotwali Dehat, due to rash and negligent driving of trailer (Tata motor 18 tyres)
bearing registration No.RJ14GG8661 being driven by respondent No.1 /Rahamdeen? (OPP)
8.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, The Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
9. Now in this case, the petitioner Abdul Salam is the injured and witness of the accident.

In order to establish his claim, petitioner Abdul Salam has examined himself as PW-1 and proved his copy of Aadhar Card Ex.PW1/1, copy of Bank passbook Ex.PW1/2 copy of chargesheet Ex.PW1/3, medical treatment documents Ex.PW1/4, MLC Ex.PW1/5, disability certificate Ex.PW1/6 and copy of my PAN card Ex.PW1/7.
He also stated on oath in the affidavit about the accident and how it was caused.
He has clearly deposed that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent no. 1, who was the driver of the truck.

He has deposed that on the fateful day i.e. he along with his brothers namely Abdul Salam and & Fahimuddin and friends Zahid & Salman were going to their home Rabupura after attending a marriage ceremony in Bulandshahar U.P by car registration no MH-14-DA-0209 and when they reached near village Sikheda, the offending vehicle registration no. RJ-14GG-8661, trailer (Tata Motors 18 tyres) was coming from Bulandshahar.
It was being driven rashly and negligently at excessive speed and dashed in the petitioner's car and other two vehicles with the forceful impact from behind.
As a result, the car fell in ditch and the offending vehicle also fall over his car.
Driver Zahid And Salman died on the spot.
He and his brothers sustained grievous injuries.
He suffered multiple injuries on his body.
Due to the forceful impact by the offending vehicle, the car of the petitioner was also damaged.

10. Last but not the least, the respondent no. 1 has not denied the accident or the involvement of his vehicle but has only said that the accident occurred due to the fault of a third vehicle - a tempo.
Although he has averred about this defence in his reply but has not proved anything in this regard.
Further, none of the respondents have led any evidence to prove anything contrary to claim of petitioner.
11. In view of above, it is proved that petitioner sustained injuries due to rash and negligent act of respondent no. 1, the driver of the offending truck.
Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.

sentences.text: 3 ISSUE NO. 2: (ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation on account of said injuries and if yes, to what extent and from whom?
Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

13. In the case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, the Hon'ble Supreme Court while delineating on the general principles relating to compensation in injury cases observed that the provisions of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 ("the Act"), for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.

sentences.text: The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following :
Pecuniary damages (Special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured , comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (General damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage).
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

sentences.text: In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under head (i), (ii) (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injuries, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the head (ii) (b), (iii), (v)
and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
Assessment of pecuniary damages under item (i) and (ii)(a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of the actuals and are easily ascertainable from evidence.
Award under the head of future medical expenses - item (iii) depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for future treatment and cost thereof.

Assessment of non-pecuniary damages - item (iv), (v) and (vi)
involves determination of lump sum amounts with reference to circumstances such as age, nature of injury, deprivation, disability suffered by the claimant and the effect thereof on the future life of the claimant.

Regarding disability, it was held by the Hon'ble Court that what requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured; and after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of income, it has to quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying the standard multiplier method to determine the loss of dependency.
14.
The Hon'ble Court further held that ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent ability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (a) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood, or (b) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (c)
whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood.
For example, if the left hand of a claimant is amputated, the permanent physical or functional disablement may be assessed around 60%.
If the claimant was a driver or a carpenter, the actual loss of earning capacity may virtually be hundred percent, if he is neither able to drive or do carpentry.

On the other hand, if the claimant was a clerk in government service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be continued as a clerk as he could perform his clerical functions; and in that event the loss of earning capacity will not be 100% as in the case of a driver or carpenter, nor 60% which is the actual physical disability, but far less.

In fact, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of 'loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in government service, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities as a consequence of losing his hand.

Sometimes the injured claimant may be continued in service, but may not found suitable for discharging the duties attached to the post or job which he was earlier holding, on account of his disability, and may therefore be shifted to some other suitable but lesser post with lesser emoluments, in which case there should be a limited award under the head of loss of future earning capacity, taking note of the reduced earning capacity.

It may be noted that when compensation is awarded by treating the loss of future earning capacity as 100% (or even anything more than 50%),
the need to award compensation separately under the head of loss of amenities or loss of expectation Abdul Salam vs . Raham Deen & Ors on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99949359/
5 of life may disappear and as a result, only a token or nominal amount may have to be awarded under the head of loss of amenities or loss of expectation of life, as otherwise there may be a duplication in the award of compensation.

sentences.text: Therefore, the compensation in this case is calculated as follows.

MEDICAL EXPENSES:
15.
Petitioner has stated in his evidence affidavit that he has spent around Rs.1,00,000/- on his medical treatment.
However, his counsel has admitted that the bills proved on record are of Rs.19,261/-.
Therefore, I award Rs.19,261/- as medical expenses to the petitioner.

PAIN AND SUFFERING:
16.
As per the affidavit of the petitioner, after the accident, petitioner was treated in AIIMS Hospital and has lost his left eye permanently.
According to the disability certificate, the petitioner has suffered 42% locomotor disability due to fracture and 30% ophthalmological disability in the left eye.
Though the petitioner has during arguments mentioned that he remained hospitalised for 7-8 days but there is no corresponding record regarding that.
The discharge summary of AIIMS shows that he was admitted there on 03.11.2020 to 04.11.2020 that was for a day.

Though, the evidence of the petitioner shows that there was no prolonged hospitalisation but the twin disabilities suffered by him, is a clear proof of the amount of pain and suffering, he must have endured in that accident.
Accordingly, I find it appropriate to grant a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- to the petitioner under this head.

LOSS OF INCOME DURING TREATMENT :
17.
Petitioner has claimed that he was running a business of repairing and manufacturing scissor and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
But he has not placed on record any proof of it.

Therefore, the income of petitioner can be considered at par with minimum wages applicable to unskilled category prevailing in the State of Uttar Pradesh at the time of accident (28.10.2020), which were Rs.8,758/-
per month.
Accordingly, the notional income of the deceased is taken as Rs.8,758/- per month.
(Manusha Sreekumar and Others vs United India Insurance Company Ltd. 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1441).

sentences.text: 18. It is not clear from the record for how much time the petitioner was unable to work.
This can only be presumed in the circumstances of the case.
Considering the kind of disability, the petitioner has incurred in the accident, it can be presumed that he must have been unable to work for at least one month.

Therefore, his loss of income for one month income is calculated as Rs.8,758 /-.
CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 19.

The petitioner has claimed Rs.40,000/- for his conveyance and Rs.1,00,000/- for special diet but he has not proved any actual expenses in relation to these heads and has not placed any material on record to substantiate the said expenses.
In the given facts and circumstances of the case, I deem it fit to grant Rs.5,000/- each to petitioner as conveyance and special diet charges.

sentences.text: Though no evidence has been led to show that petitioner had hired any attendant during his treatment and he has not claimed anything under this head.

It cannot be ignored that family members of petitioner must have had to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner for his routine activities and that would definitely suffer their work/job.

For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.
( DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
Therefore, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/- as attendant charges.
21. Thus, petitioner is granted a total compensation of Rs.15,000/- (5,000+5,000+5,000) under this head.
LOSS OF AMENITIES 22.
Further, the petitioner is granted Rs.50,000/- for loss of amenities.
LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO PERMANENT DISABILITY.
23. The next question that remains to be decided is the compensation with respect to the disability of the petitioner.
Under this head, it has to be seen that what could be the loss of future income on account of disability.

The disability certificate of Guru Teg Bahadur Hospital, Delhi Ex.PW1/6 clearly shows that the petitioner is the case of multiple disability, which is 42% locomotor disability due to fracture and 30% ophthalmological disability in the left eye.
Since the doctor has not been examined therefore there is no medical evidence to show how this disability will come in way of reducing the efficiency of the work in which the petitioner is engaged.

But considering the fact that the petitioner has locomotor disability of 42%, and ophthalmological disability as 30%, it is not difficult to assume that these disabilities will definitely affect his day-to-day life and profession.

Therefore, taking the higher percentage of disability of 42%, I presume that the petitioner must have suffered at least 21% functional disability which is half of 42%, also in carrying on with his profession.

In view of this, I am of the opinion that functional disability in relation to whole body of the petitioner must be considered as 21% for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of income of petitioner.

On the basis of the minimum wages attributed to him, the petitioner annual income shall be Rs.1,05,096/-.
24.

The copy of Aadhar card of the petitioner shows the date of birth of petitioner as 01.01.1963,
which would mean that he was around 57 years of age at the time of accident and thus, multiplier of 9 would be applicable.

Further, an addition of income of injured for future prospects to the extent of 10 % has to be considered as the age of the petitioner was between 50-60 years (National Insurance Company Limited vs Pranay Sethi and others (2017) 16 SCC 680, Pappu Dev Yadav vs Naresh Kumar and others 2010 SCC online SC 752 and Sohan Lal vs. Taj Khan & Ors., 2019 ACJ 252,
Rajasthan High Court).
